meta.description: External reference fixtures for the Merton (1974) structural credit model (KMV equity inversion, distance to default, default probability, endogenous debt spread), the Black-Cox (1976) first-passage default probability, Merton (1976) jump-diffusion European prices, and the model-level outputs built on them: CDS par spread and calibration, hazard-curve export, the Monte Carlo bond engine and merton_report.

reference_source.name: MATLAB mertonmodel documentation; Hull (2022) Example 24.3; QuantLib (Python)

extra.equity_inversion: Hull (2022), Example 24.3 (inputs, as cited by the replication); expected values from the independent Newton solve in gen_merton_golden.py, cross-checked against the R replication at https://mlozanoqf.github.io/tutorial_arf/02-merton.html
extra.jump_series: Merton, R. (1976), Option pricing when underlying stock returns are discontinuous, JFE 3
extra.cds_calibration: quote = the cds_par_spread reference (QuantLib MidPointCdsEngine) of a terminal-barrier model with the stated asset volatility; expected asset_vol is that generating volatility
extra.mc_bond: closed-form exogenous-recovery risky bond in gen_merton_golden.py: each cash coupon is paid if the firm has survived to its date, recovery_rate x notional is paid at the end of the monitoring step in which default occurs, and notional is paid at maturity on survival; all discounted at the flat rate. Survival is the Merton survival 1 - N(-d2) evaluated in gen_merton_golden.py for a terminal barrier, QuantLib AnalyticBinaryBarrierEngine hitting probability (as in black_cox) for a first-passage one. The standard error is the exact standard deviation of that discrete outcome distribution divided by sqrt(num_paths)
extra.report: default probability: Merton survival 1 - N(-d2) evaluated in gen_merton_golden.py for a terminal barrier, QuantLib AnalyticBinaryBarrierEngine hitting probability (as in black_cox) for a first-passage one; distance to default: d2; implied spread: -ln(1 - PD (1 - R)) / T; debt spread and implied equity: the Merton equations as in equity_inversion; CDS par spread: QuantLib MidPointCdsEngine as in cds_par_spread; default point: KMV short-term debt plus half of long-term debt (Crosbie & Bohn, 2003)

conventions.rates: continuously compounded annual decimals, including payout rates and dividend yields
conventions.time: year fractions; QuantLib dates are whole 365-day years under Actual/365 Fixed
conventions.valuation_date: none: every model input is a year fraction. QuantLib evaluation date 2026-01-15 only anchors its flat term structures
conventions.units: asset, equity and debt values share one currency unit; volatilities, rates, spreads and probabilities are decimals; option prices are per unit of underlying
conventions.kmv_published: debt barrier = Liability; DD and PD use the physical Drift; Maturity 1 year
conventions.equity_inversion: E = V e^{-qT} N(d1) - B e^{-rT} N(d2), sigma_E = N(d1) e^{-qT} sigma_V V / E; DD and PD are risk-neutral (d2, N(-d2)); debt spread = -ln((V e^{-qT} - E)/(B e^{-rT}))/T. The payout terms follow this crate's documented convention; only the payout_rate = 0 cases are externally anchored
conventions.black_cox: risk-neutral probability that V_t touches B e^{g t} before T, continuous monitoring
conventions.jump: dS/S = (r - q - lambda k) dt + sigma dW + (J - 1) dN, ln J ~ N(mu_jump, sigma_jump^2), k = exp(mu_jump + sigma_jump^2/2) - 1; discounted prices per unit of underlying
conventions.model_level_time: cds_par_spread, cds_calibration, hazard_curve, mc_bond and report run QuantLib on Actual/360 with 360-day years, so quarter and month steps are whole days and the year fraction of TODAY + 360 t days is exactly t
conventions.barrier_growth_rate: null is the terminal barrier (default only if V_T < B); a number g is the first-passage barrier B e^{g t}
conventions.cds_par_spread: decimal per annum. Quarterly premium grid in year fractions (no IMM dates, calendar or settlement lag); flat continuously compounded discount at the model's risk-free rate; survival probabilities on a year-fraction axis; premium accrual = year fraction x 365/360 (ACT/360 premium on an ACT/365F axis); protection and half-period accrual on default discounted at the period midpoint; recovery a fixed fraction of notional. QuantLib's Actual/360 accrual of 0.25 per quarter is mapped by dividing its par spread by 365/360
conventions.cds_calibration: terminal barrier, geometric Brownian assets; quote in basis points; asset value, barrier, rate, payout and recovery held fixed while asset volatility is solved
conventions.hazard_curve: piecewise-constant hazard, the rate of each pillar holding on (t_{i-1}, t_i]; survival queried by year fraction from the curve base date; the recovery stored on the curve does not enter survival
conventions.mc_bond: prices in percent of par, dirty. Geometric Brownian assets with drift r - q, 12 steps per year, no antithetic sampling, num_paths independent paths from the stated seed. Cash coupons of notional x coupon_rate / frequency on a regular grid ending at maturity; a coupon is paid only if the firm has survived its date. Exogenous recovery: recovery x notional paid at the end of the step in which default is recognised (maturity for a terminal barrier). First-passage default uses the engine's default Brownian-bridge crossing test, which is exact in distribution for a barrier that is flat or exponentially growing in log space. Discounting is flat at the model's risk-free rate
conventions.report: each check names a MertonReport field (index = position in the horizon vector); `rejected` lists measures the model must refuse, reported as null with an entry in `errors`. Grades are not asserted: the master scale has no external reference here. implied_equity is not asserted for a first-passage model, where equity is not a plain call

tolerances.kmv_published: half a unit of the last printed digit: 5e-5 for volatility, DD and PD (4 decimals), 500 for asset value (5 significant figures at 1e7 scale)
tolerances.equity_inversion: 1e-6 relative: the reference is converged to 1e-13; the production fixed point stops at a 1e-8 relative step
tolerances.black_cox: 5e-9 absolute: the crate's adjudicated closed-form tolerance against QuantLib's normal CDF (see vol_models_quantlib)
tolerances.jump_bates_limit: 1e-7 relative: QuantLib's own Bates-vs-Merton tolerance is 2e-8, widened for the 128-term COS expansion
tolerances.jump_quantlib_table: 1e-2 absolute: the tolerance QuantLib applies to this table, whose values are printed to 2 decimals
tolerances.jump_series: 1e-6 absolute: an a priori bound equal to the one this crate's COS-vs-Black-Scholes unit tests assert for the default 128-term expansion
tolerances.eps_pd: 5e-9 absolute on one default probability, the black_cox tolerance; the model-level tolerances below propagate it through each formula on the reference values and are fixed by the generator before any comparison
tolerances.cds_par_spread: absolute, per case: LGD x eps_pd x (1/A + P x accrual x (n + 0.5) / A^2), with P the protection sum per unit loss, A the risky annuity and n the number of quarters. A survival error of eps_pd per node moves P by at most eps_pd (Abel summation) and A by at most eps_pd x (sum of accruals + half an accrual). The QuantLib legs are asserted against a hand-written O'Kane sum at 1e-12 relative, so reference error is negligible
tolerances.cds_calibration: absolute on asset volatility, per case: the cds_par_spread tolerance divided by the reference slope ds/dsigma (central difference of the QuantLib spread, bump 1e-4), plus the solver's 1e-10 coordinate tolerance
tolerances.hazard_curve: pillars: eps_pd absolute. Off-pillar: eps_pd / S(last pillar) absolute, the bound on a log-linear interpolate of two pillar survivals each off by eps_pd
tolerances.mc_bond: three standard errors, absolute in percent of par. The standard error is not taken from the simulation: it is the exact standard deviation of the closed-form outcome distribution divided by sqrt(num_paths). default_rate uses 3 x sqrt(PD (1 - PD) / num_paths). Seed, path count and tolerance are fixed here; a miss is reported, not re-seeded
tolerances.report: per check. Default probability eps_pd; distance to default 1e-12 relative (elementary arithmetic); implied spread eps_pd x LGD / ((1 - PD x LGD) T); equity value eps_pd x (V e^{-qT} + B e^{-rT}), debt spread that divided by (D T), equity volatility sigma_E x (eps_pd / N(d1) + dE / E); CDS spread as in cds_par_spread. Equity-source checks use the equity_inversion tolerance of 1e-6 relative; the default point and barrier are exact
